title: Letters That Echo, Hide or Join
tagline: Qalqalah, the lam of ال, the connecting alif and silent letters.
intro: This level collects the rules that belong to single letters: the five letters that bounce, the lam that is silent before some letters, the alif that disappears when you join words, and letters that are written but never said.

lessons.title: Qalqalah
lessons.summary: When one of the five letters ق ط ب ج د has a sukun, release it with a small bounce.
explain: Qalqalah means shaking or echoing. The five letters ق ط ب ج د are made with a firm closure. When they carry a sukun (or you stop on them), the closure releases with a small, crisp bounce.
A classic way to remember them is the phrase قُطْبُ جَدٍّ (qutbu jadd).
Minor (sughra): the letter has a sukun in the middle of a word or phrase, as in يَجْعَلُونَ.
Major (kubra): you stop on the letter at the end of a verse, as in أَحَدٌ. Here the bounce is the strongest.
It is a light, quick bounce, not an extra vowel. Red in this course.
lessons.identify: Which rule makes this letter echo?
how: Release with a tiny bounce, without adding a vowel.
lessons.spot: Red. One of ق ط ب ج د with a sukun, or one of them at the end of a verse when you stop.
tips: Think of a tiny echo, not a bark.
mistakes: Forgetting the bounce at a verse end.

examples.note: أَحَدٌ: stop on the dal: major qalqalah.
ٱلصَّمَدُ: stop on the dal: major qalqalah.
يَلِدْ: dal with sukun mid-verse (minor); يُولَدْ: stop on dal (major).
ٱلْفَلَقِ: stop on the qaf: major qalqalah.
ٱقْرَأْ: qaf with sukun (minor); خَلَقَ: stop on qaf (major).

cards.a: ق ط ب ج د (remember: قُطْبُ جَدٍّ).

cards.q: What is the difference between minor and major qalqalah?
cards.a: Minor: the sukun is in the middle of a word/phrase. Major: you stop on the letter at the end of a verse; the bounce is strongest.

lessons.title: Sun Letters (Silent Lam)
lessons.meaning: The lam of the sun letters
lessons.summary: Before 14 'sun letters', the lam of ال is not pronounced and the next letter is doubled.
explain: The definite article ال has a lam. Before the 14 sun letters, that lam is silent and the next letter carries a shaddah: ٱلشَّمْسُ is ash-shams, not al-shams.
The 14 sun letters are ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن.
The silent lam is gray in this course, and the sun letter after it is doubled.
lessons.letters: ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن
lessons.identify: Is the lam of ال pronounced here?
how: Double the next letter, as shown by its shaddah.
lessons.spot: Gray lam, and the next letter has a shaddah.
tips: Sun letters are made near the front of the mouth where the lam is made; that is why the lam melts into them.

examples.note: وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيْتُونِ: the sun letters ت and ز.

cards.q: What happens to the lam of ال before a sun letter?
cards.a: It is silent, and the sun letter is doubled (shown with a shaddah).
ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن

lessons.title: Moon Letters (Clear Lam)
lessons.meaning: The lam of the moon letters
lessons.summary: Before 14 'moon letters', the lam of ال is pronounced clearly, with a sukun.
explain: Before the 14 moon letters, the lam is said clearly: ٱلْقَمَرُ is al-qamar.
The 14 moon letters are ا ب ج ح خ ع غ ف ق ك م ه و ي.
The lam carries a sukun and has no color, and the letter after it has no shaddah.
lessons.letters: ا ب ج ح خ ع غ ف ق ك م ه و ي
lessons.identify: Is the lam of ال pronounced here?
how: Then say the next letter normally.
lessons.spot: The lam has a sukun and the next letter has no shaddah.
tips: Every letter that is not a sun letter is a moon letter.
mistakes: Dropping the lam, as if it were a sun letter.

cards.q: How do you pronounce the lam of ال before a moon letter?
cards.a: Clearly, with a sukun: ٱلْقَمَرُ = al-qamar.
ا ب ج ح خ ع غ ف ق ك م ه و ي

lessons.title: Connecting Alif (Hamzat al-Wasl)
lessons.summary: The alif with a small head (ٱ) is pronounced only when you START on it. When joined to the word before it, it disappears.
explain: Hamzat al-wasl is the alif written with a small mark on top (ٱ). When you join the word to the previous one, you skip it: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ is bis-millah, not bismi-allah with an extra alif.
Where it appears: the article ال, commands of three-letter verbs (ٱكْتُبْ), past and command verbs of five or six letters (ٱسْتَغْفَرَ), and a few nouns like ٱسْم and ٱبْن.
It is gray in this course. How to start on it is in Level 6.
how: When joining, glide over the alif.
Only pronounce it when you begin reading on that word.
lessons.spot: Gray. An alif with a small head (ٱ) in the middle of a sentence.
tips: If it disappears, you are correct. It is a 'bridge' that only appears when needed.
mistakes: Pronouncing the alif in the middle of a sentence.

examples.note: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ: the alif of ٱللَّهِ disappears.
ٱلصِّرَٲطَ: the alif is skipped after ٱهْدِنَا.
بِٱسْمِ: the alif of ٱسْم is skipped.
ٱسْمَ: the alif is skipped after سَبِّحِ.

cards.q: When is the hamzat al-wasl (ٱ) pronounced?
cards.a: Only when you START reading on it. When joined to the previous word, it is skipped.

lessons.title: Silent Letters
lessons.summary: Some letters appear in the written text but are not pronounced. The most common is the extra alif after the waw of the plural verb.
explain: In verbs like كَفَرُوا۟ and ءَامَنُوا۟ the final alif is only a spelling convention. You read kafaru and aamanu.
The Mushaf marks such letters with a small round zero (۟) above them.
They are gray in this course: quiet letters.
how: Pronounce the waw before it as a normal 2-count madd.
lessons.spot: Gray. A letter with a small round zero (۟) above it.

cards.q: What does a small round zero (۟) above a letter mean?
cards.a: The letter is written but not pronounced.

lessons.title: Merging Two Letters
lessons.meaning: Idgham of similar and close letters
lessons.summary: When a letter with a sukun is followed by a letter from the same or a nearby spot, the first merges into the second.
explain: Mutajanisayn: two letters made at the same place but with different qualities. Examples: ت with د or ط, and ذ with ظ.
Mutaqaribayn: two letters made at nearby places. Examples: ل into ر, and ق into ك.
In both, the first letter has a sukun and the second has a vowel. The first merges into the second, and the second is doubled.
When the two letters are exactly the same (mithlayn), they also merge: for example in ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ.
how: Skip the first letter's own sound.
lessons.spot: Gold or brown. A letter with a bare sukun and a doubled letter right after it, across two words.
tips: The famous mutaqaribayn: قُل رَّبِّ. The lam merges into the ra.

cards.q: What's the difference between mutajanisayn and mutaqaribayn?
cards.a: Mutajanisayn: two letters from the SAME place (but different qualities), e.g. ت/د. Mutaqaribayn: two letters from NEARBY places, e.g. ل/ر.
